title: Modals of ability and possibility
titleVi: Động từ khuyết thiếu: khả năng và khả năng xảy ra
summary: Dùng can, could, be able to và could have done đúng ngữ cảnh — khả năng chung, thành công cụ thể và khả năng không thành.
whyItMatters: `Can` không có dạng tương lai, dạng hoàn thành hay dạng sau modal khác, nên bạn phải biết chuyển sang `be able to`. Trong Task 2, câu như *Governments will be able to...* xuất hiện liên tục; viết *will can* là lỗi khiến giám khảo dừng lại ngay.

sections.heading: can and could: general ability
body: **can + base verb** expresses present ability or possibility; **could** is its past form for general ability: *She can speak three languages. She could swim before she started school.*
Both are also used for permission and requests: *Can I borrow your notes? Could you check this paragraph?* — **could** is the more polite of the two.
**Can** has only present and past forms. Every other tense or combination needs **be able to**.

examples.right: She can speak three languages fluently.
He could swim before he started school.
Could you check the second paragraph for me?

sections.heading: be able to: where can cannot go
body: Use **be able to** after another modal, in the perfect tenses, and in the infinitive: *will be able to*, *have been able to*, *might be able to*, *want to be able to*.
**Could** cannot be used for a single success in the past. For one specific achievement, use **was/were able to** or **managed to**: *The fire spread quickly, but everybody was able to escape.*
The negative **couldn't** works in all past contexts, including single events: *I couldn't finish the test on time.*

examples.right: By 2030, the city will be able to recycle 70% of its waste.
examples.note: Future ability → **will be able to**, never **will can**.

examples.right: Despite the flooding, all residents were able to leave safely.
examples.note: One specific past success → **were able to**.

examples.right: I haven't been able to reach the supplier all week.
examples.wrong: I haven't could reach the supplier all week.

examples.right: The team managed to finish the survey before the deadline.

sections.heading: could for possibility and suggestion
body: Beyond ability, **could** expresses a present or future possibility that is less certain than **can**: *The story could be true* (= it is possible).
It is also the natural modal for suggestions: *We could go to the cinema* — softer than *We can go*.
Use **could**, not **can**, for unrealistic or imagined situations: *I could sleep for a week.*

rows: She was able to pass the test.
She will be able to apply next year.

sections.heading: could have done: an unrealised past possibility
body: **Could have + past participle** means something was possible in the past but did not happen: *You could have stayed with us — we had a spare room.*
The negative **couldn't have + V3** means something would not have been possible: *She couldn't have known about the delay.*
Do not confuse it with **was able to**. *I could have passed the exam* means I had the ability but did not take or pass it; *I was able to pass the exam* means I actually passed.

examples.right: You could have stayed with us — we had a spare room.
She couldn't have finished the report in one evening.
We could have taken the earlier train, but we missed it.
examples.wrong: We could take the earlier train, but we missed it.
examples.note: Possibility trong quá khứ không thành → **could have taken**.

sections.heading: Accuracy rules for IELTS writing
body: Modals are followed by the **base verb** with no *to*: *can speak*, never *can to speak*. The single exception is **ought to** and **have to**, which are not true modals.
Never combine two modals: *will can*, *might could*, *must can* are all impossible. Replace the second modal with **be able to** or a lexical verb.
In Task 2, **be able to** is the standard way to talk about future capacity: *Remote work will enable employees to...* / *Companies will be able to recruit globally.*

examples.right: Remote work will enable companies to recruit globally.
examples.note: Lexical alternative to a double modal.

examples.right: Students might be able to sit the exam online next year.
examples.wrong: Students might can sit the exam online next year.
examples.note: Hai modal không đứng cạnh nhau → **might be able to**.

examples.right: The scheme could reduce commuting costs significantly.

commonMistakes.wrong: Students will can access the library online.
commonMistakes.right: Students will be able to access the library online.
commonMistakes.why: Không dùng hai modal liền nhau. `Can` không có dạng tương lai nên phải thay bằng `be able to`.

commonMistakes.wrong: I could pass the driving test last month.
commonMistakes.right: I was able to pass the driving test last month.
commonMistakes.why: `Could` chỉ diễn tả khả năng chung trong quá khứ. Một thành công cụ thể dùng `was/were able to` hoặc `managed to`.
Sau modal là động từ nguyên mẫu không có `to`. Đây là lỗi rất phổ biến của người học Việt Nam.

commonMistakes.wrong: I could have went to the conference.
commonMistakes.right: I could have gone to the conference.
commonMistakes.why: Sau `could have` phải là quá khứ phân từ (V3), không phải quá khứ đơn.

commonMistakes.wrong: He hasn't could find a job.
commonMistakes.right: He hasn't been able to find a job.
commonMistakes.why: Thì hoàn thành không đi với `could`; cấu trúc đúng là `have/has been able to`.

ieltsTips: Khi nói về năng lực trong tương lai ở Task 2, dùng `will be able to` hoặc động từ thường như `enable`, `allow`, `permit` thay vì cố gắng ghép `will can`.
Dùng `could` để giảm nhẹ đề xuất trong bài thảo luận: `One solution could be to subsidise public transport.`
Trong Speaking Part 3, phân biệt `could` (khả năng chung) với `was able to` (thành công cụ thể) khi kể trải nghiệm — giám khảo chú ý sự chính xác này.
Dùng `could have + V3` để nêu giải pháp đã bị bỏ lỡ: `The city could have avoided the congestion by investing earlier.`

exercises.question: Despite the storm, all passengers ___ leave the airport safely.
exercises.explanation: Một thành công cụ thể trong quá khứ → **were able to**.

exercises.question: Which sentence expresses future ability correctly?
options: Students will can study online next year.
Students will be able to study online next year.
Students will can to study online next year.
Students will be able study online next year.
exercises.explanation: Không ghép hai modal; dạng tương lai của **can** là **will be able to**.

exercises.question: You ___ stayed with us — we had a spare room.
exercises.explanation: Khả năng trong quá khứ nhưng không xảy ra → **could have + V3**.

exercises.question: Which sentence means the person actually succeeded?
options: I could finish the report yesterday.
I was able to finish the report yesterday.
I could have finished the report yesterday.
I might finish the report yesterday.
exercises.explanation: **was able to** = đã làm được thật; **could have finished** = đã có thể nhưng không làm.

exercises.question: Which sentence uses 'can' correctly?
options: She can to speak three languages.
exercises.explanation: Sau modal dùng động từ nguyên mẫu không có **to**, và modal không chia **-s**.

exercises.question: By 2040, the country ___ (be able) to generate half its electricity from renewables.
exercises.explanation: Tương lai của **can** là **will be able to**; ở đây động từ **be able** đứng trước **to generate**.

exercises.question: I ___ (not / be able) to contact the supplier since Monday.
exercises.explanation: Thì hoàn thành phủ định của **be able to** là **haven't been able to**.

exercises.question: The team ___ (manage) to complete the survey before the deadline.
exercises.explanation: **manage to + V** diễn tả thành công cụ thể; chia quá khứ đơn.

exercises.question: You ___ (could / not / know) about the change — nobody told you.
exercises.hint: khả năng không thể trong quá khứ
exercises.explanation: Điều không thể xảy ra trong quá khứ → **couldn't have + V3**.

exercises.question: One practical solution ___ (could) be to subsidise public transport.
exercises.explanation: **Could** giảm nhẹ mức độ chắc chắn khi nêu giải pháp trong Task 2.
